findings.description: This bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so stored objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are not guaranteed to be encrypted with a managed or customer-managed key.
No ACL is declared and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so there is nothing preventing a public ACL or bucket policy from exposing its contents.
The bucket has no logging block, so object access to this data bucket is not recorded for audit or incident investigation.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably, defeating tamper-resistance of stored records.
The ledger export bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted at rest by explicit configuration.
No public access block is attached; the private ACL alone does not prevent a later bucket policy or ACL change from making the ledger data public.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so reads and writes of ledger exports leave no S3 access audit trail.
The model artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving it open to accidental public exposure via ACL or policy.
Operational runbooks, which frequently contain sensitive procedural and connection detail, are stored in a bucket with no server-side encryption configuration.
No logging block is configured, so access to the runbooks bucket is not auditable.
No public access block resource restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket.

The audit/log-delivery bucket sets force_destroy = true and has no public access block or object lock, so the central audit trail can be destroyed by a terraform apply and is not protected against ACL/policy-based exposure.
A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/business data) is uploaded from the repository into an unencrypted bucket with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument set.
